title: Eaton vs. Corning: Which Industrials Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
author: Brendan Coffey
description: The article compares Eaton Corp. and Corning Inc. as potential industrial stock investments for 2027. Eaton, with 10% revenue growth and a lower P/E ratio of 33.67, benefits from electrification and data center trends with strong order backlogs. Corning, showing 19% revenue growth and ambitious plans to reach $40 billion in sales by 2030 through AI data center deals, trades at a premium P/E of 43.06 but offers greater long-term growth potential. The author ultimately favors Corning for 2027 despite its higher valuation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong execution on electrification megatrends, record backlogs, 28% Q3 sales growth, 12-year data center order backlog, and expected 20%+ sales growth in 2026 with 12% growth projected for 2027. Lower valuation (P/E 33.67) provides conservative entry point.

Impressive 19% revenue growth, 60% net income increase in Q3 2026, major deals with Meta, Nvidia, and Amazon for AI data centers, ambitious Springboard program targeting $40 billion sales by 2030, and reduced Apple dependency through new AI customers. Author's preferred choice despite premium valuation.

title: 3 AI Infrastructure Stocks to Buy Hand Over Fist if the Market Pulls Back
author: Micah Zimmerman
description: Despite recent market volatility and AI stock selloffs, three infrastructure companies supporting the data center boom—Eaton, Corning, and Emcor—reported record quarters with strong outlooks. All three trade significantly below 52-week highs, presenting buying opportunities as their order books and contracts indicate continued growth well into 2027.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Data center revenue rose 65% last quarter with orders more than doubling. Operating margins improved significantly, capacity expansion projects are 72% complete, and management raised full-year guidance for the third time. Stock trades 26% below 52-week high.

Optical fiber sales jumped 44% to $2.38B with AI product sales more than doubling. Signed four multibillion-dollar long-term customer deals that share capacity costs. Generated $2.27B in adjusted free cash flow while expanding. Stock trades 58% below 52-week high with expected 36% earnings growth.

Record remaining performance obligations of $18.57B, up 47% year-over-year, driven by data center work. Data center mechanical revenue more than doubled. Raised 2026 guidance, added $500M buyback authorization, and acquired P1 Construction with minimal debt. Stock trades 31% below 52-week high.
Mentioned as context for market volatility (CEO resignation on Nov. 12) but not the focus of the article. The author specifically notes the three recommended stocks don't depend on which chip wins.

title: Eaton vs. Vertiv: Which Industrials Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
author: Brendan Coffey
description: Eaton and Vertiv are both industrial companies benefiting from electrification and AI-driven data center demand. Eaton, a diversified power management giant with $27.4B in FY2025 revenue, offers more stability with lower valuations. Vertiv, a specialized cooling and power systems provider, shows stronger growth with 27.7% revenue growth and 44% projected 2026 growth, but carries higher valuation multiples. The article concludes Eaton edges out as the better buy for 2027 due to slightly cheaper P/E and P/S ratios, though both present compelling opportunities.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong diversified business with $27.4B revenue, 10.3% YoY growth, solid 14.9% net margin, moderate debt levels (0.6x D/E), record backlogs extending 12 years, Q3 2026 sales up 28%, and lower valuation multiples (P/E 25.8x, P/S 4.3x) make it the article's recommended choice for 2027.

Exceptional growth profile with 27.7% FY2025 revenue growth, 44% projected 2026 growth, strong positioning in AI data center cooling market, strategic partnerships with Microsoft and Amazon, and 13% net margin. However, higher valuations (P/E 35.29x, P/S 5.7x) and concentration risk in data center spending limit it as a secondary choice.

title: Why a Data Center Slowdown Would Reach Utilities and Electrical Suppliers Before Chipmakers
author: Manali Pradhan, Cfa
description: Recent voter restrictions on data center development in 40 of 41 local ballot contests could delay construction projects, affecting utilities and electrical equipment suppliers before impacting chipmakers. Utilities like American Electric Power may need to postpone infrastructure investments, while electrical suppliers with strong order backlogs could weather near-term weakness. Chipmakers like Nvidia may continue benefiting from existing data center upgrades, though prolonged delays pose longer-term risks.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Data center construction delays would postpone AEP's planned $100 billion infrastructure investments through 2031, slowing future earnings growth and reducing rate base expansion opportunities, though current electricity sales to existing customers would be less immediately affected.

Strong backlog of $26.2 billion with 72% targeted for delivery within 12 months provides near-term revenue protection despite potential slowdown in new data center orders. However, prolonged weakness could eventually pressure earnings growth and valuation at 26x expected 2026 earnings.

Chipmakers may avoid immediate impact as customers continue upgrading existing facilities and installing chips at alternative locations. However, prolonged construction delays could eventually affect chip demand if data center capacity constraints persist, creating risks around Nvidia's $279 billion in supply commitments.

Microsoft's recent $45.2 billion capital expenditure (75% on chips and hardware) demonstrates continued strong chip spending despite data center construction delays, suggesting resilience in near-term demand for semiconductor purchases.

title: Eaton Stock Declines More Than 7% in 6 Months: Time to Buy the Dip?
author: Na
description: Eaton Corporation (ETN) has underperformed its industry by 7.6% over six months due to margin pressures and premium valuation concerns, despite raising 2026 organic growth guidance to 13%-15% and adjusted EPS guidance to $13.70-$13.80. The company benefits from data center demand, strategic acquisitions, and capacity expansions, but analysts recommend a wait-and-see approach given the elevated valuation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Eaton demonstrates strong structural growth drivers (data center expansion, grid modernization, AI demand) and raised guidance multiple times, the stock's premium valuation (22.30X forward P/E) and recent 7.6% underperformance warrant caution. The Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating reflects balanced growth prospects offset by valuation risks.
Emerson Electric gained 22.5% over six months, outperforming the industry average of 0.2%, indicating positive market sentiment and stronger relative performance compared to peers.
Powell Industries declined 42.5% over six months, significantly underperforming both the industry and peers, indicating substantial negative market sentiment.
